props.gloss_en: [the mishna's] for both this and that but not for cisterns, ditches and caves -- you find it where heavy rain and gentle rain came, but not much came
the baraita: [rain] fell for cisterns, ditches and caves, but not for this and that
how can you find it? where it came in a downpour
they sound the alarm over trees [until] near Pesach
over cisterns, ditches and caves [until] near the Festival
and if they have no water to drink, they sound the alarm over them at once
and what is their 'at once'? Monday, Thursday and Monday
and over all of them they sound the alarm only in their own district
and askara: when there is death in it, they sound the alarm over it
they sound the alarm over askara when there is no death in it -- which the baraita denies (when there is no death in it, they do not)
and they sound the alarm over the govai in any amount
they sound the alarm over the chagav too -- R' Shimon ben Elazar's 'even over the chagav'
they sound the alarm over trees in the other years of the septennate
over cisterns, ditches and caves even in the Sabbatical year
they sound the alarm over trees in the Sabbatical year too -- RSBG's 'even over trees in the Sabbatical year'
RSBG's reason (19b.8): because they hold sustenance for the poor
they sound the alarm over aftergrowths in the Sabbatical year
the reason (19b.9): because they hold sustenance for the poor
from the day the Temple was destroyed, rains became meagre [tzimukin] for the world
there is a year whose rains are many and a year whose rains are few; a year whose rains fall in their time and a year whose rains do not
a year whose rains fall in their time is like a servant whose master gave him his rations on Sunday: the dough is baked properly and eaten properly
a year whose rains do not fall in their time is like a servant given his rations on Friday: the dough is baked improperly and eaten improperly
a year whose rains are many is like a servant given his rations all at once: the mill [loses] from a kor what it [loses] from a kav, and the dough likewise
a year whose rains are few is like a servant given his rations little by little: what the mill [loses] from a kor it [loses] from each kav, and the dough likewise
alternatively: [a year] whose rains are many is like one who kneads clay -- with much water the water is not used up and the clay is well kneaded; with little, the water runs out and the clay is not
once all Israel went up to Jerusalem for the festival and had no water to drink
Nakdimon to the hegmon: lend me twelve wells of water for the pilgrims and I will give you twelve springs of water; and if I do not, I will give you twelve talents of silver
Nakdimon: I still have time; the whole day is mine (and at noon and at mincha: I still have time in the day)
the hegmon, mocking: all year no rain fell, and now rain will fall?!
Nakdimon's prayer: Master of the world, it is revealed and known before You that I did not act for my honour nor my father's house's, but for Yours, that water be available to the pilgrims
at once the sky was bound with clouds and rain fell until the twelve wells were filled and overflowed
Nakdimon to the hegmon: give me the price of the excess water you owe me
the hegmon: I know the Holy One shook His world only for you, but I still have a claim on you to take my money -- the sun had already set, and the rain fell in my possession
Nakdimon's second prayer: Master of the world, make known that You have beloved ones in Your world
at once the clouds scattered and the sun shone
the hegmon: had the sun not broken through, I would have had a claim on you to take my money
a tanna taught: his name was not Nakdimon but Buni
and why was he called Nakdimon? because the sun broke through for him
the baraita: the sun broke through for Moshe (one of three)
the baraita: the sun broke through for Yehoshua (one of three)
the baraita: the sun broke through for Nakdimon ben Guryon (one of three)
Yehoshua -- a verse too, as it is written 'and the sun stood still and the moon stayed' (Josh 10:13)
R' Yochanan: 'who shall hear the report of you and tremble and be in anguish because of you' (Deut 2:25) -- when did they tremble and were in anguish? when the sun broke through for Moshe
R' Yochanan: [Moshe's case] comes from the verse itself (Deut 2:25)

אתיא תת תת: here 'I will begin to put [tet] the dread of you' (Deut 2:25), there 'on the day the Lord put [tet] the Amorites' (Josh 10:12)
